why: Variable window, the longest valid: the window is valid while it contains at most k zeros (each zero can be flipped). Grow the right end every step; when the zero count exceeds k, shrink from the left until it is valid again; the answer is the largest valid window.
hints: Rephrase: what does a stretch of ones after at most k flips look like in the original array?
It is a contiguous window with at most k zeros. Extending right only adds zeros; moving left only removes them.
Two pointers: for each right, count zeros; while zeros > k, drop nums[left] and left += 1; best = max(best, right - left + 1). O(n).
pitfalls: k = 0 is the longest run of existing ones.
k can be at least the number of zeros: the answer is then n.
Shrink with while, not if, in the general template (here if also works, but while is the habit to build).
